edition.en: Excerpts from Chapter VIII of Passages from the Life of a Philosopher (London, 1864), as transcribed on English Wikisource; omitted passages are marked with a section break, and the misprint 'impossibilty' is corrected.
edition.zh: 据英文维基文库所录《一位哲学家的生平片段》（伦敦，1864 年）第八章节选；省略处以分隔线标出；改正了一处误排（impossibilty）。

basis.en: Published in 1864; Charles Babbage died in 1871.
basis.zh: 1864 年出版；作者卒于 1871 年。

note.en: Babbage wrote these memoirs at seventy-two, still hoping the Analytical Engine would be built; this excerpt from his chapter on it keeps his own account of the store and the mill, the punched cards borrowed from the Jacquard loom, and his generous record of Lovelace's notes. Notice the line that the engine 'will possess a library of its own': every set of cards, once made, can be run again. That is the idea of a program as something kept and handed on.
note.zh: 巴贝奇七十二岁时写下这部回忆录，仍盼着分析机能够造成；这里节选其中论分析机的一章，保留了他本人对“存储器”与“运算器”、借自提花织机的穿孔卡片的说明，以及他对洛夫莱斯注释的慷慨记述。请留意那句“分析机将拥有一座自己的图书馆”：每一组卡片一经制成，就能再次运行。这正是把程序当作可以保存、可以传下去的东西的想法。

excerpt.orig: Thus the Analytical Engine will possess a library of its own.
excerpt.en: Thus the Analytical Engine will possess a library of its own.
excerpt.zh: 这样，分析机将拥有一座自己的图书馆。
